title: Triangulations as a discretization of the gravity sum
notes: The notes replace an integral over metrics on the sphere by \(Z(\beta)=\sum_n\sum_{\Gamma_n}e^{-\beta n}\), allowing generalized triangulations, and say forbidding exceptional gluings does not change the answer.
statement: For a specified finite class of connected oriented maps dual to cubic ribbon graphs, define a formal area-generating series with symmetry weights \(1/|\operatorname{Aut}\Gamma|\). Changes between unrestricted maps and simple triangulations alter coefficients and the critical coupling; in the pure-gravity universality class their leading susceptibility exponent agrees. This does not construct a measure on all smooth metrics.
reconstruction: Orientation, connectedness, symmetry weights, and the distinction between exact coefficients and a universal exponent are supplied editorially.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2 and 4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} already derive the planar generating series. The continuum gravity interpretation is developed in \citet{polyakov1981quantum}; no equality of measures is proved in these notes.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Formal cubic Hermitian matrix integral
notes: \(I(g)=\int e^{-\operatorname{tr}(U^2+gU^3/\sqrt N)}dU\), followed by \(Z=\lim N^{-2}\log I(e^{-\beta/2})\).
statement: Expand the cubic exponential formally against a normalized Gaussian measure and use \(N^{-2}\log[I(g)/I(0)]\) for connected vacuum graphs. For real nonzero \(g\), the displayed real integral diverges along one scalar direction. A convergent complex-contour definition requires additional data and is not implied by the formal power series.
reconstruction: The formal interpretation and division by \(I(0)\) repair the displayed expression; they are not extra claims attributed to Kazakov.
fate: \citet[Sec. 4, Eq. (42)]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} explicitly states the instability of the cubic integral and uses its formal series. The notebook suppresses both this qualification and Gaussian normalization.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Wick contractions and the genus power of N
notes: A six-factor Gaussian moment is illustrated by one contraction; double lines make closed index loops contribute \(N\), and a graph is assigned \(N^{F-V/2}=N^{2-2\chi}\), with \(\chi\) called its Euler number.
statement: For a Gaussian Hermitian matrix with density proportional to \(e^{-\operatorname{tr}U^2/2}\), \(\mathbb E(U_{ij}U_{kl})=\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\); every even moment sums over all pairings. A connected cubic ribbon graph has \(3V=2E\), so its power is \(N^{F-E+V}=N^{2-2g}\), where \(g\) is genus. With density \(e^{-\operatorname{tr}U^2}\), the covariance has an additional factor \(1/2\).
reconstruction: The missing pairing sum, index order, Gaussian scaling, and genus/Euler-characteristic distinction are explicit editorial repairs.
fate: The topological expansion is the pre-existing large-\(N\) method of \citet{thooft1974planar}; \citet[Sec. 2]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} specializes it to matrix counting.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Eigenvalue reduction and the Vandermonde square
notes: Writing \(U=\Omega\Lambda\Omega^{-1}\) changes the matrix integral into an eigenvalue integral with \(\prod_{i<j}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^2\).
statement: Lebesgue measure on complex Hermitian matrices decomposes, away from repeated eigenvalues, as \(C_N\Delta(\lambda)^2\prod_i d\lambda_i\,d\bar\Omega\), with angular measure on \(U(N)/U(1)^N\); ordering and permutation factors are absorbed in \(C_N\). For invariant integrands the angular factor cancels in normalized ratios.
fate: \citet[Sec. 3]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} uses precisely this reduction. It is standard Weyl integration rather than a new matrix-gravity theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Uniform equilibrium density in the circular ensemble
notes: Dyson\textquotesingle s circular ensemble is mentioned as a case in which the limiting density is constant.
statement: For Haar-distributed unitary matrices, the normalized one-point eigenangle density is constant on the circle; the corresponding large-\(N\) logarithmic-gas equilibrium measure is normalized Lebesgue measure. This concerns the circular ensemble with no external potential; the Hermitian cubic model has a nonconstant equilibrium density.
fate: \citet[Sec. IV, Thm. 6; Sec. V, Thm. 8 and Eq. (79)]{dyson1962statistical} defines the Haar unitary ensemble and its circular eigenangle density. The original paper, received 15 September 1961 and published in 1962, was opened and these results read. The exact source used by the speaker is not identified.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Exact cubic free-energy series and critical radius
notes: The notes give \(-\frac12\sum_{k\ge1}(72g^2)^k\Gamma(3k/2)/[\Gamma(k/2+1)(k+2)!]\), then write \(g_c=1/(108\sqrt3)\).
statement: In the source normalization \(\operatorname{tr}(U^2/2+gU^3/\sqrt N)\), the negative planar logarithm has the displayed series and its nearest singularity in \(g^2\) is \(g_c^2=1/(108\sqrt3)\). The notebook\textquotesingle s earlier quadratic coefficient is different, so one must either restore \(U^2/2\) or rescale \(g\). The coefficients are weighted connected maps with \(2k\) cubic vertices.
reconstruction: Normalization is compared to the original paper; the series cannot simultaneously use the notebook\textquotesingle s unrescaled quadratic term and the source\textquotesingle s critical constant.
fate: \citet[Sec. 4, Eqs. (49)--(52)]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} is an exact pre-1986 match, including the squared critical coupling.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Pure-gravity singular exponent and map asymptotics
notes: \(Z(\beta)\sim(\beta-\beta_c)^{5/2}\) and map coefficients have an \(n^{-7/2}\) factor.
statement: The nonanalytic part of the unrooted connected planar free energy has exponent \(5/2\). Transfer to coefficients gives a \(k^{-7/2}\) power multiplying exponential growth, with vertex parity and coupling conventions retained. Analytic background terms are present; rooting a map changes the power by a factor proportional to its number of edges.
reconstruction: The words nonanalytic part, weighted unrooted count, and parity qualification are editorially necessary.
fate: The cubic solution in \citet[Sec. 4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} supplies this singularity. Record 695 clarifies why unlabelled integer counts are not the coefficients of the raw free energy.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Adding spins to the random surface
notes: The final paragraph proposes putting a second kind of variable, including spins, on the triangulation.
statement: The annealed partition function sums both over maps and over matter configurations on each map. An Ising field on a cubic dual graph can be encoded by two matrix species with a covariance coupling different spins.
fate: Kazakov develops this construction in record 685 and in \citet{kazakov1986ising}; no independently specified conjecture occurs in this closing remark.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the Ising-on-random-map model is solved in the planar limit; this does not identify every possible added matter system.

title: KdV as the Euler equation on the Virasoro group
notes: KdV is described as an Euler equation on the Virasoro group, extending the familiar Euler equation for a Lie group.
statement: For the Virasoro central extension of vector fields on the circle, the Euler--Arnold equation of the right-invariant \(L^2\) metric is, up to choices of signs and scale, \(u_t+3uu_x+c u_{xxx}=0\). The fixed dual central coordinate produces dispersion; the metric and coadjoint convention are indispensable.
reconstruction: The metric, fixed central coordinate, and coefficient convention are supplied rather than read from the one-line note.
fate: \citet[Prop. 1]{ovsienkokhesin1987super} proves the Euler interpretation of KdV and then constructs the super-extension in Proposition 2. The manuscript was received 8 August 1986 and published in 1987; this is the directly matching near-contemporary publication.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Euler equations on the Neveu--Schwarz and Ramond superalgebras
notes: The report adds the supersymmetric KdV equations and names the Schwarz and Ramond algebras.
statement: The super Euler construction uses an inertia pairing with an inverse derivative on the odd component. In the Neveu--Schwarz case the antiperiodic odd modes have no zero mode, so this pairing is nondegenerate. In the Ramond case the periodic odd zero mode gives a degenerate pairing and must be treated accordingly. The component fields have their stated even and odd Grassmann parities; replacing odd fields by commuting scalar functions changes the equation.
reconstruction: The name Neveu--Schwarz, the inverse-derivative inertia, and the different zero-mode behavior are supplied from the publication. The one-line notebook report preserves no explicit component system.
fate: \citet[Prop. 2 and the subsequent Ramond remark]{ovsienkokhesin1987super}, received 8 August 1986 and published in 1987, gives the directly matching construction, including the degeneracy qualification.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: An involutive Yang--Baxter symmetry
notes: A linear map \(S:L\otimes L\to L\otimes L\) satisfies \(S^2=1\) and \(S_1S_2S_1=S_2S_1S_2\).
statement: Let \(L\) be finite-dimensional over a characteristic-zero field. An involution \(S\) satisfying the braid equation determines representations of every symmetric group on \(L^{\otimes n}\), by acting in adjacent tensor factors; dropping involutivity gives braid-group representations.
fate: \citet[pp. 797--799]{gurevich1986yangbaxter} introduced this generalized formal Lie-theoretic framework before the manuscript talk: the note was received 10 April 1985 and published in 1986.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: Braided antisymmetry, Jacobi identity, and bracket covariance
notes: Three identities for the bracket are given in right-acting operator notation: antisymmetry, a three-term Jacobi identity, and a compatibility relation with \(S\).
statement: In a symmetric monoidal category with symmetry \(S\), a Lie object has a morphism \(b:L\otimes L\to L\) satisfying \(bS=-b\) and the categorical Jacobi identity. On ordinary vector spaces the further compatibility that \(b\) is a morphism for the specified tensor symmetry is essential; a bare pair consisting of any Yang--Baxter operator and any antisymmetric bracket is insufficient.
reconstruction: The categorical formulation avoids silently reversing the notebook\textquotesingle s right-acting products; the bracket covariance is retained as a separate hypothesis.
fate: \citet[pp. 798--800]{gurevich1986yangbaxter} states the corresponding generalized Lie identities. The notebook is a compressed exposition of that theory, not an independent new axiom system.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: Ordinary and super Lie algebras as examples
notes: The flip gives ordinary Lie algebras; a signed flip determined by degrees gives superalgebras.
statement: For the ordinary flip \(S(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x\) the axioms recover Lie algebras. For a \(\mathbb Z/2\)-graded space, \(S(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x\), with a parity-preserving bracket, gives super antisymmetry and super Jacobi. The degree of a nonzero homogeneous bracket is \(|x|+|y|\) modulo two.
reconstruction: Additivity of parity is a condition on homogeneous brackets, not a definition of the bracket of arbitrary nonhomogeneous vectors.
fate: These are the foundational examples recalled in \citet[pp. 798--799]{gurevich1986yangbaxter}; Lie superalgebras were already established well before 1986.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: Color symmetries and color brackets
notes: \(S(t_i\otimes t_j)=a(i,j)t_j\otimes t_i\), with conditions on \(a\) said to follow from the axioms; the notes cite Trostel, Journal of Mathematical Physics 25(11), 1984.
statement: For an abelian grading group \(G\), a bicharacter \(\varepsilon:G\times G\to k^\times\) satisfying \(\varepsilon(g,h)\varepsilon(h,g)=1\) defines such an involutive symmetry. A homogeneous bracket of degree zero then satisfies \(\varepsilon\)-skew symmetry and the corresponding color Jacobi identity. Arbitrary coefficients \(a(i,j)\) need compatibility with the degrees and nonzero structure constants.
reconstruction: The grading group and bicharacter supply one standard precise realization of the displayed coefficients; the notes do not specify them.
fate: The notebook citation is identifiable as \citet{trostel1984color}, pp. 3183--3189. The publisher metadata matches the year, volume, issue, and subject; it does not establish the uncertain attribution to Mosolov elsewhere in the line.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: The braided commutator of an associative algebra
notes: An associative algebra produces a generalized Lie bracket by subtracting the product with reversed factors through \(S\).
statement: If \((A,\mu)\) is an associative algebra object in the symmetric tensor category defined by an involutive braiding \(S\), then \(b=\mu-\mu S\) is a Lie object. Associativity alone, combined with an unrelated solution of the braid equation, does not suffice: multiplication must be compatible with the braiding.
reconstruction: The compatibility hypothesis is explicit in the modern statement; the brief notebook sentence leaves it implicit.
fate: \citet[pp. 799--800]{gurevich1986yangbaxter} treats associative and Lie objects in the same compatible setting.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: Historical attribution of braiding formalism to Drinfeld
notes: The notes say that Drinfeld put braids in their final form.
statement: This sentence records a historical assessment; it does not specify a theorem, construction, or priority claim precise enough to adjudicate. The mathematical identities actually present are indexed separately.
fate: Gurevich\textquotesingle s 1986 paper provides a concrete contemporaneous source for the adjacent mathematics, but no exact publication is identified with this informal phrase.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the phrase remains an insufficiently specified historical attribution; no open mathematical problem is inferred.
speaker: D. I. Gurevich

title: Annealed Ising model on cubic planar maps
notes: Spins \(\sigma_i=\pm1\) are summed on the vertices of a random dual graph, with edge interaction and magnetic field.
statement: For each connected cubic map \(\Gamma\), use \(Z_\Gamma(\beta,H)=\sum_{\sigma}\exp[\beta\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\sigma_i\sigma_j+H\sum_i\sigma_i]\), then sum over maps with a specified area and automorphism weight. Each unoriented edge is counted once. This is an annealed ensemble: summing over geometry is part of the partition function.
reconstruction: Edge counting and symmetry weights remove otherwise ambiguous factors in the notebook expression.
fate: \citet{kazakov1986ising}, published December 1986, exactly solves a closely related planar Ising matrix model. \citet{boulatovkazakov1987ising} develops the magnetic-field critical behavior; its preprint circulated in 1986.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Continuum Majorana field coupled to gravity
notes: The model is associated with a fermionic field and gravity; the notes emphasize that the continuum identification is difficult.
statement: The critical Ising matter theory is the Majorana conformal field theory with central charge \(1/2\). Its coupling to random planar maps has continuum gravitational critical exponents. A formal identification of a discrete annealed partition sum with a path integral over metrics and Grassmann fields is not, by itself, an equality of rigorously defined measures.
reconstruction: The central charge and the distinction between discrete exact solvability and continuum measure construction are editorial context.
fate: The matrix solution of \citet{kazakov1986ising} and its extension in \citet{boulatovkazakov1987ising} establish exact discrete planar results; their interpretation as matter coupled to gravity is a further continuum argument.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the Ising-gravity universality class and its exponents are established; the notebook supplies no precise measure-convergence theorem to classify separately.

title: Two-matrix encoding of Ising edge weights
notes: The integral has a mixed quadratic term \(-2cUV\) and cubic terms \(g(e^HU^3+e^{-H}V^3)/\sqrt N\), with \(c=e^{-2\beta}\).
statement: Use two Hermitian Gaussian matrices with covariance proportional to \(\begin{pmatrix}1&c\\c&1\end{pmatrix}\), for \(|c|<1\), and expand the cubic terms formally. A propagator between different species carries weight \(c\) relative to equal species. Multiplication by a common edge factor converts this to \(e^{\beta\sigma_i\sigma_j}\). Cubic integrals on a real contour remain formal unless contours are specified.
reconstruction: The covariance, positivity restriction, and common edge rescaling are supplied; the notebook uses an unnormalized quadratic form.
fate: This is the matrix-model mechanism of \citet{kazakov1986ising} and \citet{boulatovkazakov1987ising}. A quartic model enumerates maps of a different valency and has different critical couplings.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Critical Ising coupling on cubic random maps
notes: The transition is at \(\beta_*=\frac12\log(2\sqrt7+1)\).
statement: For the standard cubic two-matrix Ising model at zero magnetic field, the matter critical point has \(c_*=e^{-2\beta_*}=(2\sqrt7-1)/27=1/(2\sqrt7+1)\). This is a joint critical point of matter and the map-generating function, not the fixed square-lattice Ising temperature.
reconstruction: The zero-field cubic-map normalization is necessary to identify the constant.
fate: The cubic critical constant is checked against the explicit Boulatov--Kazakov model in \citet[Eq. (2.9)]{sato2020ising}; its antecedent is \citet{boulatovkazakov1987ising}. The 1986 quartic-lattice paper alone is not an exact match for this numerical constant.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Wick theorem as an all-pairings identity
notes: Varchenko explains that the Gaussian moment is the sum of products of pairwise covariances; odd moments vanish.
statement: For centered jointly Gaussian variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_{2m}\), \(\mathbb E\prod_iX_i=\sum_{\pi}\prod_{\{a,b\}\in\pi}\mathbb E(X_aX_b)\), where \(\pi\) runs over all perfect matchings; moments of odd total degree are zero. Repeated variables are allowed. The matrix version is obtained by substituting its covariance.
fate: This is the classical Gaussian pairing theorem used by \citet[Sec. 2]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar}. The intervention explains the mechanism rather than proposes a new theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: A. N. Varchenko

title: Expansion coefficients and Gaussian index contraction
notes: The expansion is written with Gaussian moments of powers of traces; the displayed contractions and Taylor coefficients are compressed.
statement: The formal identity is \(\langle e^{-gP}\rangle_0=\sum_{n\ge0}(-g)^n\langle P^n\rangle_0/n!\). Hermitian entry contractions cross the indices, \(\langle U_{ij}U_{kl}\rangle_0\propto\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\). Logarithms select connected diagrams, with automorphism weights remaining after the factorials are included.
reconstruction: Taylor factorials and covariance orientation are restored explicitly; these are repairs to the displayed shorthand.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2--4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} supplies the relevant expansion and graph conventions. These details explain the rational, rather than unlabelled integer, coefficients stressed later in record 695.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Discriminant complements and the braid group
notes: Roots are replaced by coefficients \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n\); the discriminant is removed, and the fundamental group is identified with the group of braids.
statement: The space of monic complex polynomials of degree \(n\) with simple roots is the unordered configuration space of \(n\) points in \(\mathbb C\), hence has fundamental group \(B_n\). The ordered root space is its \(S_n\)-cover and has pure braid group as fundamental group. The universal punctured-plane fibration has fiber \(\mathbb C\setminus\{z_1,\ldots,z_n\}\).
fate: The topological construction underlying the Burau representation is recalled in \citet[Sec. 2]{bigelow1999burau}; it was classical before this report.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Rank-one twisted cohomology and reduced Burau
notes: The multivalued function \(f^\alpha\), where \(f(z)=\prod(z-z_i)\), defines coefficients for first cohomology; moving the roots gives a braid representation.
statement: Let \(t=e^{2\pi i\alpha}\ne1\) be the common local monodromy about each puncture. Then \(H^1(\mathbb C\setminus\{z_i\},\mathcal L_t)\) has dimension \(n-1\). Monodromy in the configuration space gives the reduced Burau representation, up to duality and basis conventions. The universal form is over \(\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]\), and specializing \(t\) is a separate operation.
reconstruction: The nontrivial local-monodromy hypothesis and separation of formal parameter from exponent are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2]{bigelow1999burau} uses the equivalent infinite-cyclic-cover construction. It verifies the representation being discussed, but not the notebook\textquotesingle s attribution of every step to Givental.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The Hecke quadratic relation and parameter conversion
notes: The braid generator is said to satisfy \((T_i+1)(T_i-\alpha)=0\), although \(\alpha\) has just denoted the exponent of \(f\).
statement: For the conventional Burau generator \(B_i\), \((B_i-1)(B_i+t)=0\). With \(T_i=-B_i\), this becomes \((T_i+1)(T_i-t)=0\). Thus the Hecke parameter is the multiplicative monodromy \(t\), not the additive exponent \(\alpha\); inverse conventions can replace \(t\) by \(t^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The displayed polynomial is reconciled by an explicit normalization, not silently copied.
fate: The universal representation and its matrices are stated in \citet[Sec. 1]{bharathrambirmanbrendle2026burau}; the notebook\textquotesingle s formula is consistent only after a parameter renaming and sign convention.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Faithfulness of the Burau representation
notes: The stated goal is to prove faithfulness; the case \(n=3\) is already known.
statement: For which \(n\) is the universal reduced Burau representation \(B_n\to\operatorname{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}])\) injective? This concerns the indeterminate-parameter representation and does not assert faithfulness at every complex specialization.
reconstruction: The original all-rank question is separated from the exceptional rank-four case and from specialized representations.
fate: \citet[Theorem 1.1]{bigelow1999burau}, first posted 20 April 1999 and published in 1999, proves nonfaithfulness for \(n\ge5\). \citet[Main Theorem, Sec. 1]{bharathrambirmanbrendle2026burau}, posted 6 July and revised 14 September 2026, claims faithfulness for \(n=4\). Its actual theorem and PDF were read; the proof has not been independently certified in this project.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, faithfulness for \(n\le3\) and nonfaithfulness for \(n\ge5\) are established; \(n=4\) has a recent affirmative preprint claim, which must be identified as such. The unrestricted conjecture in the notes is false.

title: Hyperelliptic monodromy specialization
notes: The final line says \(\alpha=-1\) yields monodromy of elliptic or hyperelliptic integrals.
statement: The double-cover interpretation corresponds to local monodromy \(t=-1\), hence exponent \(\alpha\in\frac12+\mathbb Z\) if \(f^\alpha\) is used. Its periods lie in the appropriate anti-invariant part of homology of the branched double cover; compactification and parity of the number of branch points affect the dimension.
reconstruction: The distinction between exponent \(-1\), which has trivial monodromy, and multiplicative parameter \(-1\) resolves the apparent contradiction.
fate: The Burau-cover description in \citet[Sec. 2]{bigelow1999burau} supports the specialization, but the notebook conflates the exponent and its exponential.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Hodge--de Rham degeneration in characteristic zero
notes: For a smooth projective complex variety, the spectral sequence from coherent differential forms to de Rham cohomology degenerates.
statement: For a smooth proper variety \(X\) over a characteristic-zero field, \(E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)\Rightarrow H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{p+q}(X)\) degenerates at \(E_1\). Over \(\mathbb C\), algebraic de Rham cohomology identifies with singular cohomology with complex coefficients; projective smoothness also supplies the classical Hodge decomposition.
reconstruction: The indexing is standardized and smooth proper is distinguished from the more restrictive projective hypothesis in the note.
fate: The statement predates the seminar. \citet[Introduction and Cor. 2.4]{deligneillusie1987relevements} gives a new algebraic proof through reduction to positive characteristic, published in 1987.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Lifting modulo p squared and the truncated Cartier splitting
notes: The notes credit a new algebraic proof to Deligne and Illusie, with a preprint at Orsay.
statement: If \(X\) is smooth over a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\) and lifts smoothly to \(W_2(k)\), then the truncated Frobenius pushforward \(\tau_{<p}F_*\Omega_X^\bullet\) splits in the derived category as \(\bigoplus_{i<p}\Omega^i_{X^{(1)}}[-i]\). For proper \(X\) with \(\dim X<p\), this yields full Hodge--de Rham degeneration. Characteristic-zero degeneration follows by spreading out and choosing suitable large primes.
reconstruction: The lifting, perfectness, truncation, and dimension hypotheses are not present in the brief report and are reconstructed from the theorem.
fate: \citet[Thm. 2.1 and Cor. 2.4]{deligneillusie1987relevements} is the precise matching result. The notebook witnesses circulation by October 1986; the article appeared in Inventiones 89 (1987), 247--270.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The normalized Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber integral
notes: The unitary integral of \(\exp\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda U M U^*)\) is a determinant of exponentials divided by two Vandermondes.
statement: For Hermitian \(A,B\) with eigenvalues \(a_i,b_j\) and normalized Haar measure, \[\int_{U(N)}e^{t\operatorname{tr}(AUBU^*)}\,dU=\left(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}k!\right)t^{-N(N-1)/2}\frac{\det[e^{ta_i b_j}]}{\Delta(a)\Delta(b)}.\] Initially take distinct eigenvalues and \(t\ne0\); all apparent singularities extend by continuity. The same Vandermonde ordering is used in numerator conventions for both spectra.
fate: \citet[Eq. (3.12)]{itzyksonzuber1980planar} gives the directly matching matrix formula, building on Harish-Chandra\textquotesingle s earlier orbital-integral work. The author-hosted original PDF and formula were inspected.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Principal-minor integral and shifted spherical parameters
notes: Gelfand recalls an integral of complex powers of successive principal minors and attributes it to Gelfand--Naimark, 1951.
statement: For \(R>0\), principal minors \(\Delta_k\), \(s\in\mathbb C^N\), and \(s_{N+1}=0\), average \(\prod_k\Delta_k(URU^*)^{s_k-s_{k+1}}\). If \(a_j=s_j+N-j\), the value is \(\bigl(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}k!\bigr)\det[r_i^{a_j}]/[\Delta(r)\Delta(a)]\). Positive minors fix the logarithms; colliding parameters are handled by limits.
reconstruction: The exact principal-minor exponents and Weyl shifts repair the compressed notebook display.
fate: The old formula and its original book locator are reproduced with proof in \citet[Prop. 2.1]{faraut2014rayleigh}. Record 692 gives a fuller representation-theoretic explanation. The shifts \(N-j\) must not be dropped.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Radial heat operator on Hermitian matrices
notes: The heat equation on the real vector space of Hermitian matrices becomes a radial equation in eigenvalues; multiplication by the Vandermonde makes it free.
statement: With the Hilbert--Schmidt Euclidean metric on \(\operatorname{Herm}_N\), a conjugation-invariant smooth function has radial Laplacian \(\Delta(\lambda)^{-2}\sum_i\partial_i[\Delta(\lambda)^2\partial_i]\). Conjugation by \(\Delta\) gives \(\Delta^{-1}\sum_i\partial_i^2\Delta\). The radial heat kernel is therefore an antisymmetrized product of scalar Gaussian kernels after accounting for the Jacobian.
reconstruction: The metric fixes heat-time and Gaussian normalization; smooth continuation through collisions is understood.
fate: \citet[Sec. 3, Eqs. (3.13)--(3.17)]{itzyksonzuber1980planar} gives this derivation. It is specific to the complex Hermitian, or Dyson-index-two, radial operator; analogous real and quaternionic operators retain interaction terms.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Berezin and Harish-Chandra antecedents of the radial method
notes: Gelfand says Berezin had obtained the result and Harish-Chandra used it repeatedly.
statement: This intervention links the matrix heat calculation to the radial-part method in harmonic analysis. It does not identify a unique dissertation proposition; the exact unitary integral and its radial proof are indexed separately.
fate: \citet{berezingelfand1956spherical} is a verified pre-1986 primary source for spherical-function harmonic analysis. The notebook\textquotesingle s particular dissertation attribution is retained as a historical recollection, not upgraded to a proved priority assertion.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the mathematical antecedent is established, but the precise dissertation passage intended by this intervention is not identified.

title: A unitary integral with two coupled external-source pairs
notes: The question is to evaluate \(\int e^{\operatorname{tr}(A_1UB_1U^*)+\operatorname{tr}(A_2UB_2U^*)}\,dU\), related in the notes to a chiral field.
statement: For fixed finite matrices, the exponential has an absolutely convergent Taylor expansion on the compact group. Each coefficient is a finite sum of unitary moments computable by Weingarten calculus. In general the two-source exponent does not reduce to one HCIZ pair; an all-coupling planar asymptotic formula is a stronger question than finite-dimensional evaluability.
reconstruction: The convergent finite-\(N\) method is an editorial application of the integration theorem; it is not asserted to be the speaker\textquotesingle s intended closed formula.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2, Cor. 2.4]{collinssniady2006integration}, first circulated February 2004 and published 2006, gives all polynomial Haar moments, hence an exact coefficientwise method. The notebook does not specify the source scaling needed to identify a unique large-\(N\) chiral-field problem. This is the same integral family as 1986-695.11 and 1986-698.1. \ours\ The chapter gives an exact \(N=2\) formula, a convergent finite-\(N\) moment expansion with a remainder bound, and a three-source obstruction to treating relative angles as independent.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 finite-\(N\) evaluation by a convergent moment series is available. The vague chiral-field identification is not treated as a separate solved or open theorem.

title: Analytic solution of reduced planar gauge integrals in dimensions three and four
notes: The integral is underlined as unevaluated, and gauge theory as unsolved.
statement: Determine the large-\(N\) free energy and Wilson-loop observables of a precisely normalized \(d\)-matrix reduced gauge model for \(d=3,4\), through its phases, and establish the regime in which these observables reproduce the extended-lattice theory. Solving a finite compact integral by Taylor expansion is not this nonperturbative planar problem.
reconstruction: The free-energy scaling, observables, and distinction between the unrepaired original model and symmetry-preserving variants make the question precise.
fate: The reduction of \citet{eguchikawai1982reduction} is a reformulation, not a general analytic solution. \citet[Secs. 1--2]{garciaperez2020largeN} describes continuing numerical work; \citet{neuberger2020quenched} distinguishes competing quenching prescriptions. Neither proves an all-coupling solution of the notebook integral.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 exact two-dimensional results and controlled reductions/numerics do not provide the requested general three- or four-dimensional planar solution. The original untwisted weak-coupling equivalence is false, and must be repaired before a continuum-physics claim.
worth: Worth developing only after fixing a model and phase; a bounded strong-coupling coefficient calculation or symmetry test is feasible, whereas an all-coupling solution is not a bounded project.

title: Heat-kernel proof of the unitary orbital formula
notes: The report starts from \(g_t=\Delta g\) on Hermitian matrices and states the determinant formula for the orbital integral.
statement: Compare the full Euclidean heat kernel on \(\operatorname{Herm}_N\) with its radial kernel after multiplication by \(\Delta(\lambda)\). Antisymmetrization over eigenvalue permutations yields the determinant of scalar heat kernels and therefore HCIZ, normalized by the value at a scalar matrix.
fate: This is the method already given in \citet[Sec. 3]{itzyksonzuber1980planar}; it repeats 1986-688.3 with a new exposition.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Spectrum of a product of positive Hermitian matrices
notes: Given the spectra of \(H_1,H_2>0\), the notes ask how the spectrum of \(H_1H_2\) is distributed.
statement: The product is similar to \(H_1^{1/2}H_2H_1^{1/2}>0\). Two different questions must be distinguished: which eigenvalue lists occur, and the pushforward distribution when relative eigenvectors have Haar law. The first is a multiplicative spectral-support problem; the second needs a specified measure and cannot be answered by support inequalities alone.
reconstruction: Haar-relative-eigenbasis sampling is supplied as the natural precise probabilistic interpretation; the note does not explicitly choose it.
fate: \citet{klyachko2000random} relates product singular-value support to additive Hermitian spectral inequalities. Principal-minor spherical transforms, as in \citet[Sec. 2]{faraut2014rayleigh}, are relevant to the distribution question. Neither reference is claimed to be the exact unstated density formula intended in the note.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 finite-dimensional spectral support has established solutions; the notebook\textquotesingle s unspecified distribution question is not identified with one universal density theorem.

title: Ellipsoid sections and interlacing arrays
notes: A plane section of an ellipsoid with axes \(a,b,c\) is described by \(a\le a_1\le b\le b_1\le c\); repeated sections form a triangular array.
statement: For a Hermitian operator restricted orthogonally to a codimension-one subspace, sorted eigenvalues interlace. Repeated principal compressions produce Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns. For ellipsoids, the quadratic-form eigenvalues are inverse squared semiaxes; the inequality must be translated consistently if the symbols denote geometric lengths.
reconstruction: Compression, axis convention, and ordering are supplied.
fate: \citet[Thm. 1.1 and Prop. 2.3]{faraut2014rayleigh} states the interlacing theorem and orbital-measure pushforward. The geometric interlacing is classical; the modern probability formulation is context, not a 1986 novelty attribution.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Principal-minor powers as spherical coordinates for integration
notes: The next integral averages powers of \(a_{11}\), a leading \(2\times2\) determinant, and successive minors of \(U^*\mu U\).
statement: For positive definite \(\mu\), these complex powers are unambiguously defined using positive real logarithms. Their unitary average is the spherical function of \(\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)/U(N)\); the exponent differences and \(N-j\) shifts are as in 1986-688.2 and 1986-692.1.
reconstruction: Positivity of \(\mu\) is needed for the elementary complex-power interpretation.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2, Prop. 2.1]{faraut2014rayleigh} reproduces the Gelfand--Naimark integration scheme. This occurrence motivates the representation-theoretic explanation given on 3 November.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The numerical equatorial-slab assertion in dimension 1000
notes: The question asks what fraction of a 1000-dimensional ball lies in a layer of thickness \(R/100\) about an equator; the answer written is almost all.
statement: For uniform volume in the radius-\(R\) ball of dimension \(d\), \(\Pr(|x_1|\le aR)=I_{a^2}(1/2,(d+1)/2)\). At \(d=1000\), even the generous half-width interpretation \(a=0.01\) gives approximately \(0.248\); interpreting \(R/100\) as total thickness gives approximately \(0.126\). Thus the literal numerical example does not illustrate almost-full concentration.
reconstruction: Two possible meanings of thickness are tested rather than choosing one silently.
fate: The formula follows from the cross-sectional volume of a ball. \oursComputed\ The numerical values are independently checked by quadrature and the regularized beta function in the accompanying code; this is an editorial correction, not a new concentration theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the general concentration heuristic is standard, but this specific dimension-to-width ratio is quantitatively false.

title: Time spent near faces of a high-dimensional simplex billiard
notes: A particle reflects at faces of a 1000-dimensional simplex; the notes say it spends almost all time within \(1/100\) of the faces.
statement: The statement does not specify units for the boundary layer, the shape or inradius of the simplex, initial-condition measure, or whether the assertion is an ensemble or almost-every-trajectory limit. Concentration of volume near a boundary alone cannot establish a time-average claim without a suitable dynamical hypothesis.
reconstruction: The required data are identified without replacing the notebook sentence by an invented general billiard conjecture.
fate: No definite billiard theorem can be matched to these missing quantifiers. The neighboring ball question explains the heuristic motivation, but supplies neither ergodicity nor a trajectorywise argument.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this occurrence is underdetermined; no open problem or class-D inference is made.

title: Diagonal projection as a moment map and its Fourier transform
notes: On Hermitian matrices with fixed eigenvalues, take \(H\mapsto\operatorname{diag}H\); the Fourier transform is written down.
statement: On the coadjoint orbit of \(U(N)\) with its Kirillov--Kostant--Souriau form, diagonal projection is the moment map for the diagonal torus. Its image is the convex hull of permutations of the fixed eigenvalue list. The Fourier transform of the pushed-forward normalized orbital measure is \(\int e^{i\operatorname{tr}(D U\Lambda U^*)}\,dU\), hence HCIZ with \(t=i\).
reconstruction: The symplectic form, measure normalization, and Schur--Horn image describe the standard precise construction; the note only states the map and transform.
fate: \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation} supplies the general moment-map measure context; \citet[Sec. 3]{itzyksonzuber1980planar} supplies the explicit Fourier integral. These were pre-existing results.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Exact stationary phase for a Hamiltonian circle action
notes: For a closed symplectic manifold and periodic Hamiltonian flow, the first stationary-phase term is said to give the exact integral. The written prefactor is \((2\pi)^{-n}\), without a signature phase.
statement: Let \((M^{2n},\omega)\) be compact without boundary and let \(H\) generate a circle action with isolated fixed points. With Liouville measure \(\omega^n/n!\), the oscillatory integral is exactly its stationary-phase sum. In local Darboux coordinates, for real \(t>0\), each point contributes \((2\pi/t)^n e^{itH(p)}e^{i\pi\operatorname{sgn}(\operatorname{Hess}_pH)/4}/\sqrt{|\det\operatorname{Hess}_pH|}\). Consistent orientation and moment-map conventions fix signs.
reconstruction: Isolated nondegenerate fixed points, the Liouville factorial, absolute determinant, signature phase, and \(t\)-scaling are supplied.
fate: \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation} proves exactness; \citet[Thm. (1.5)]{duistermaatheckman1983addendum} treats nonisolated fixed sets. The notebook calls its own formula approximate, appropriately, but its displayed constant and phases cannot be retained literally.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Coadjoint-orbit symplectic form and the unitary integral
notes: For \(X=U^*\mu U\), the form is written \(\omega(X)(\xi,\eta)=\operatorname{tr}(X[\xi,\eta])\), with \(\xi,\eta\) called tangent vectors.
statement: If tangent vectors are represented by infinitesimal generators \(\xi,\eta\) as \(\operatorname{ad}^*\xi X,\operatorname{ad}^*\eta X\), the orbit form is \(\omega_X(\operatorname{ad}^*\xi X,\operatorname{ad}^*\eta X)=\langle X,[\xi,\eta]\rangle\), up to a uniform sign. It descends modulo the stabilizer; generators are not literally arbitrary tangent matrices. A regular unitary orbit is \(U(N)/U(1)^N\); repeated eigenvalues enlarge the stabilizer.
reconstruction: The generator/tangent distinction and regular-orbit qualification repair the notation.
fate: This is the orbit example of exact localization in \citet{duistermaatheckman1982variation}; the resulting alternating exponential sum agrees with HCIZ in \citet{itzyksonzuber1980planar}.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Higher stationary-phase terms and characteristic numbers
notes: Gelfand asks when the second term vanishes, when the first term is exact, and how characteristic numbers can arise.
statement: Within compact Hamiltonian torus geometry, localization on a fixed component integrates the exponential of the restricted symplectic form divided by the equivariant Euler class of its normal bundle. Curvature expansions produce characteristic classes and a finite-degree contribution on each component. Outside a specified Hamiltonian phase-amplitude class, vanishing of one coefficient does not characterize exactness.
reconstruction: The compact Hamiltonian subclass is distinguished from the unbounded scope of the informal question.
fate: \citet[Thm. (1.5) and its expansion on pp. 154--155]{duistermaatheckman1983addendum} already gives the fixed-component and characteristic-class mechanism. It is a precise partial answer to the intervention, not a classification of all oscillatory integrals.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the localization answer in the specified subclass is established. The note does not define a general classification problem beyond it.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The note-taker proposes replacing the circle by a nilpotent group
notes: The sentence begins \ru{Гипотеза (моя)} and suggests a nilpotent Lie-group action, with a two-dimensional example expected to give two asymptotic terms.
statement: No Hamiltonian, phase, measure, compactness condition, fixed-point behavior, or asymptotic parameter is specified. A group action by itself does not determine the number of nonzero stationary-phase terms. The dimension-two nilpotent case is abelian, so even the proposed mechanism is not determined by a nonabelian example.

title: The principal-minor spherical integral in full normalization
notes: The integrand is a product of powers of leading principal minors of \(URU^*\); the answer has alternating powers of eigenvalues and parameter differences.
statement: Let \(r_i>0\), \(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_i)\), and \(a_j=s_j+N-j\). For normalized Haar measure, \[\int_{U(N)}\prod_{k=1}^N\Delta_k(URU^*)^{s_k-s_{k+1}}dU=\frac{\bigl(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}k!\bigr)\det[r_i^{a_j}]}{\Delta(r)\prod_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)},\quad s_{N+1}=0.\] Both eigenvalue and parameter collisions have removable limits; all complex powers use positive bases.
reconstruction: The exact normalization, exponent differences, and Weyl shifts reconstruct the abbreviated formula.
fate: \citet[Prop. 2.1, citing Gelfand--Naimark, II.9.3]{faraut2014rayleigh} gives this formula with proof. The original theorem predates 1986 by decades.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Contraction from spherical functions to HCIZ
notes: The notes say formula (2), the exponential orbital integral, follows from the first formula.
statement: With fixed Hermitian \(X\), let \(R_\tau=I+X/\tau>0\) for sufficiently large \(\tau\), and replace the spherical parameters by \(\tau s\). The principal-minor powers tend to an exponential whose exponent telescopes to \(\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{diag}(s)UXU^*)\). Compactness permits passage under the integral; the determinant side has the corresponding confluent limit.
reconstruction: The scaling and positivity range are editorial reconstruction of the indicated implication.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2, after Prop. 2.2]{faraut2014rayleigh} states precisely this Mehler--Heine-type limit. It explains the relation asserted in the notebook without claiming that the limit calculation was written there.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Characters, highest weights, and spherical matrix coefficients
notes: For integral parameters the formula is related to Weyl\textquotesingle s character formula; arbitrary complex parameters are interpreted through representations of \(\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)\).
statement: Dominant integral highest weights give Schur characters, expressed by the alternant divided by a Vandermonde. Averaging a highest-weight coefficient gives a normalized spherical function on \(\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)/U(N)\). Complex continuation defines the spherical family, but arbitrary complex inducing parameters do not give unitary representations.
reconstruction: The distinction between polynomial highest weights, analytic continuation, and the unitary parameter range is supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2]{faraut2014rayleigh} verifies the spherical formula; its shifts explain the character relation. Unitarity must be checked separately and is discussed for \(\operatorname{GL}_N\) in record 697.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Which integrals are evaluations of spherical functions?
notes: Gelfand asks which other integrals can be evaluated in this representation-theoretic way.
statement: The note specifies neither a class of integrands nor an admissible group and representation construction. A precise finite family is given by principal-minor averages and their orbital-integral limits, but a classification of all integrals having some representation-theoretic realization is not a defined question.
fate: The adjacent formulas are established examples; \citet[Secs. 2--3]{faraut2014rayleigh} explains their common harmonic-analytic origin. No exact later theorem is matched to the unrestricted wording.

title: The two compatible Poisson structures of KdV
notes: The notes write \(P_1=-2\partial\) and \(P_2=-\frac12\partial^3-u\partial-\partial u\), then ask about quantization.
statement: On local differential-polynomial functionals of a smooth periodic field \(u\), or with boundary conditions eliminating integration-by-parts terms, \(P_1,P_2\) define compatible Hamiltonian operators. Every constant linear combination is Poisson. Appropriate Hamiltonians and rescaling of \(u,x,t\) give the KdV hierarchy; coefficients cannot be compared across conventions without the rescaling.
reconstruction: The class of functionals and boundary conditions are supplied; the notebook does not fix a functional-analytic phase space.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2--3]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} surveys the classical structures with proofs, following the Gelfand--Dickey theory. The Russian original appeared in 1984, the English translation in 1985.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: A simultaneous quantization with two Planck constants
notes: Two compatible brackets suggest two Planck constants.

In the displayed classical pencil, shifting \(u\) by a constant changes \(P_2\) by a multiple of \(\partial\), so independence of two quantum parameters is not automatic.

notes: Gelfand says that genuinely nonlinear quantization is not understood, mentions quantum groups and a perturbation of a measure; Drinfeld contrasts approaches associated with Faddeev and Albeverio--Høegh-Krohn.
