title: The second bracket as the Virasoro Lie--Poisson structure
notes: Fourier expansion of the second bracket yields the Virasoro algebra and Kirillov\textquotesingle s orbit picture.
statement: The affine hyperplane of fixed central coordinate in the dual Virasoro algebra has a Lie--Poisson bracket of the form \(a\partial^3+2u\partial+u^{\prime}\), up to sign and scale. Quantization replaces the Fourier-mode Poisson brackets by Virasoro commutators. This identifies the algebra of fields; it does not by itself order the nonlinear Hamiltonians.
reconstruction: The chapter fixes the standard convention \([L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\); the notebook uses a different index/sign convention.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2]{ovsienkokhesin1987super} recalls the already known Virasoro Lie--Poisson identification; \citet[Eq. (2), (11)--(14)]{bazhanovlukyanovzamolodchikov1996integrable} separates it from the quantum charges.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Classical local commuting KdV Hamiltonians
notes: The integrals \(F_n\) are said to commute, and a quantum analogue is attributed to Zamolodchikov.
statement: For a scalar second-order Lax operator, residues of appropriate odd half-integer powers produce local functionals forming a Poisson-commutative hierarchy. They are defined modulo total derivatives; periodicity or decay makes their integrals well defined. Classical commutativity does not imply commutativity after an arbitrary ordering of modes.
reconstruction: The formal pseudodifferential convention and total-derivative quotient are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} gives the classical residue construction. The quantum question is separated as GP-1986-32.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Quantization of the full family of local KdV integrals
notes: The closing question 1(a) asks to quantize the KdV integrals; an earlier line says Zamolodchikov has quantum analogues.
statement: Construct local normally ordered Virasoro charges \(I_{2k-1}\) deforming the classical KdV Hamiltonians, with \([I_{2k-1},I_{2l-1}]=0\), rather than merely quantizing the underlying bracket. The construction is naturally formal or generic in the deformation parameter; specialized representations and convergence need separate treatment.
reconstruction: The normalization and formal/generic meaning of quantization are supplied. No assertion that an arbitrary ordering works is attributed to the notes.
fate: \citet[Thm. 4.7.3, with the generic-parameter hypotheses of Sec. 4.7.1]{feiginfrenkel1996integrals} proves deformation and commutativity in the relevant affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) case (1993 circulation; final arXiv version September 1995; publication 1996). \citet[Eq. (11) and quantum monodromy construction]{bazhanovlukyanovzamolodchikov1996integrable} gives explicit initial charges and transfer operators (1994 circulation; 1996 publication).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the algebraic construction of commuting quantum KdV charges is established. Their simultaneous spectral classification is a separate, only partly resolved problem.

title: Miura transformation and the Heisenberg Poisson field
notes: The substitution \(u=v^{\prime}-v^2\) is called Poisson for the second Gelfand--Dickey bracket, with a derivative-of-delta bracket on \(v\).
statement: For the displayed normalization \(P_2=-\frac12\partial^3-u\partial-\partial u\), take \(P_v=\frac12\partial\). The differential of the Miura map is \(D=\partial-2v\), and \(DP_vD^*=P_2\). If \(P_v=\partial\), the pushforward is \(2P_2\). This is an identity of formal Hamiltonian differential operators; global surjectivity on smooth periodic fields is not asserted.
reconstruction: The explicit factor \(1/2\) is an editorial normalization check, not a claim that the handwritten Heisenberg coefficient had that value. \ours\ The displayed Hamiltonian-operator identity and its factor \(1/2\) are checked directly in the saved symbolic calculation.
fate: \citet[Sec. 3.7]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} treats the Miura Poisson realization. The factor depends on the bracket normalization, which the notebook does not keep consistently fixed.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Normal-ordered free-boson realization of Virasoro
notes: The modes of the Heisenberg field are used to form quadratic \(L_n\); the displayed sum has only \(p>q\).
statement: With \([a_m,a_n]=m\delta_{m+n,0}\), the normally ordered modes \(L_n=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}:a_{n-k}a_k:\) act on a Heisenberg Fock module and satisfy Virasoro at \(c=1\). A background-charge derivative changes the central charge. Omitting the diagonal term when \(n=2k\), or omitting normal ordering and zero-mode data, does not give the same operator.
reconstruction: The conventional \(c=1\) realization is stated exactly; the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted sum is replaced by its required completion and ordering.
fate: \citet[Secs. 4.2 and 4.4]{feiginfrenkel1996integrals} develops the Heisenberg vertex-algebra realization; \citet[Eq. (31)]{bazhanovlukyanovzamolodchikov1996integrable} uses the corresponding quantum Miura field. The construction itself predates the report.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Higher-order scalar operators and Miura factorization
notes: \(L=\partial^n+u_{n-2}\partial^{n-2}+\cdots+u_0=(\partial+v_1)\cdots(\partial+v_n)\), with \(\sum v_i=0\), is associated with \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\), Wilson, Drinfeld, and Sokolov.
statement: Expanding the ordered product defines a differential-polynomial map from \(n\) first-order fields with sum zero to the coefficients of a monic scalar operator without its \(\partial^{n-1}\) term. The ordering matters because \(\partial f=f\partial+f^{\prime}\). Reversing the map may require a differential-field extension or local solutions; it is not an unconditional global factorization over the original smooth periodic coefficient ring.
reconstruction: The forward construction is distinguished from the stronger, generally obstructed global inverse statement.
fate: \citet[Sec. 3.7, Prop. 3.26]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie} supplies the generalized Miura setting. The reference to Picard--Vessiot theory in the notes is consistent with the field-extension qualification.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The nonlinear W3 algebra and higher quantum Miura fields
notes: The \(n=3\) second bracket gives a nonlinear algebra; Fateev, Zamolodchikov, and a Feigin report in April 1986 are mentioned.
statement: The principal quantum \(W_3\) algebra has generating fields of spins two and three whose operator products close nonlinearly through normally ordered composites. It is the \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) instance of quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction. This is different from a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with bilinear structure constants.
reconstruction: The \(W_3\) identification is strong, but the notes do not contain its full operator-product coefficients.
fate: \citet{fateevzamolodchikov1987z3} publishes the matching spin-three symmetry; \citet{feiginfrenkel1990quantization} gives the general \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\) BRST interpretation. The precise content of Feigin\textquotesingle s April conference remark is not separately recoverable.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Sklyanin and quantum KdV on a finite interval
notes: One line mentions Sklyanin\textquotesingle s quantum KdV on a finite interval with boundary conditions.
statement: No endpoint conditions, Hamiltonian, reflection matrix, or representation are specified. Periodic quantum KdV cannot simply be substituted for this boundary problem.
fate: The quantum inverse-scattering context is documented by \citet{bazhanovlukyanovzamolodchikov1996integrable}, but it is not an exact publication match for the unrecorded boundary conditions. The occurrence remains unidentified.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 no precise interval problem is determined by the surviving sentence.

title: The sweep method as a Riccati or Miura transformation
notes: Gelfand considers \(y^{\prime\prime}-a(x)y=0\), propagates \(y^{\prime}+\alpha y=0\), and writes \(\alpha^{\prime}-\alpha^2=0\) with an exclamation mark.
statement: On an interval where a chosen solution does not vanish, \(\alpha=-y^{\prime}/y\) satisfies \(\alpha^{\prime}-\alpha^2=-a\). Conversely this Riccati equation yields the factorization \(\partial^2-a=(\partial-\alpha)(\partial+\alpha)\). Zeros of \(y\) create Riccati poles; propagation must then change charts or use a matrix first-order system.
reconstruction: The omitted forcing \(-a\), zero-free interval, and chart limitation are supplied.
fate: The factorization mechanism is the scalar Miura construction discussed in \citet[Sec. 3.7]{drinfeldsokolov1985lie}. \ours\ The corrected sign and nonzero right-hand side follow directly by differentiating \(-y^{\prime}/y\); the scan confirms that zero is the actual notebook reading.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Higher-order and elliptic boundary propagation
notes: Gelfand says the sweep method also works in higher order and sketches shrinking a contour for \(\Delta u=0\), mentioning Keldysh.
statement: Higher-order scalar ODEs can be converted to first-order systems and boundary subspaces propagated by their fundamental solution. For elliptic PDEs, contour propagation leads to boundary operator families and is not the same finite-dimensional Riccati equation. The note gives no domain, regularity, solvability, or operator formula for the PDE version.
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional ODE content is separated from the unidentified PDE claim.
fate: The ODE part is standard and compatible with the factorization context of \citet{drinfeldsokolov1985lie}; no exact Keldysh theorem is identified with the elliptic sketch.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the ODE propagation mechanism is established; this specific elliptic-boundary assertion lacks sufficient data for assessment.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Feigin: invariant forms, Casimirs, and loop algebras
notes: Feigin writes the quadratic Casimir \(\sum e_i e^i\), loop \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\), and scalar products obtained from coefficients of \(\operatorname{tr}(uv)\); higher Casimirs are linked to Gelfand--Dickey Hamiltonians.
statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate invariant symmetric form, dual bases define a central quadratic Casimir in its enveloping algebra. On the loop algebra, coefficient or residue pairings \(\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{tr}(u(z)v(z))z^m dz\) are invariant. Higher invariant polynomials, after Hamiltonian reduction, give classical \(W\)-fields; quantum versions require normal ordering and corrections.
reconstruction: Nondegeneracy, invariance, and the distinction between central finite-dimensional Casimirs and reduced local fields are supplied.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2.4 and 4.6]{feiginfrenkel1996integrals} explains the classical and quantum reductions. The bare Casimir construction is old; the exact unpublished formula allegedly given in April is not filled in.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: B. L. Feigin

title: Spectrum of quantum KdV charges on irreducible Virasoro modules
notes: Question 1(b) asks to calculate the spectrum in irreducible representations of the Virasoro algebra, immediately after quantizing the KdV integrals.
statement: Fix \(c,h\in\mathbb C\), the irreducible highest-weight module \(L(c,h)\), and normalized commuting local KdV charges. Determine their joint generalized eigenspaces and nilpotent actions grade by grade, and a complete all-grade parameterization where available. An ordinary eigenbasis requires semisimplicity, which is not automatic outside a positive unitary setting.
reconstruction: The spectrum is read as the spectrum of the quantum KdV family, not merely \(L_0\). The highest-weight restriction and generalized-eigenspace target are modern specifications absent from the notebook.
fate: \citet[Eq. (11)]{bazhanovlukyanovzamolodchikov1996integrable} supplies explicit charges and a spectral program. The opened v1 of \citet[Defs. 6.5--6.6, Prop. 6.7, Thm. 6.8, Sec. 7]{masoeroruzza2026odeim} gives a 2026 preprint completeness theorem at \(c=-2\), \(h=(\beta^2-1)/8\), \(\beta\notin\mathbb Z\), for admissible QQ solutions modulo entire-function gauge, and diagonalizes the first three charges in its free-field realization. This does not settle arbitrary \(c,h\).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the general formulation remains only partly resolved. \oursComputed\ This chapter computes the level-two charge and proves a nonunitary Jordan block at \(c=1,h=-1/32\) survives in the irreducible quotient; the result is explicitly a bounded calculation, with no historical novelty claim.
worth: Worth a bounded development: exact low-grade matrices and singular-vector quotient checks reveal semisimplicity obstructions without claiming all-grade completeness.

title: Quantization of the general second Gelfand--Dickey bracket
notes: Question 2 asks for quantization of the second Gelfand--Dickey bracket in the general case.
statement: For monic scalar differential operators of order \(n\), with the \(\partial^{n-1}\) coefficient removed, construct a vertex or completed mode algebra deforming the second Adler--Gelfand--Dickey Poisson algebra. In the principal \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\) setting this is the quantum \(W_n\) algebra; the precise reduction and deformation parameter must be specified.
reconstruction: The scalar principal-reduction setting is the strongest explicit setting supported by the preceding \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\) discussion.
fate: \citet{feiginfrenkel1990quantization} identifies quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction of affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\) with \(W_n\). \citet[Thm. 4.6.9 and Sec. 4.6.10]{feiginfrenkel1996integrals} proves the more general simple-Lie-algebra construction and explains its BRST relation.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the algebraic quantization in the principal scalar-operator setting is established. This statement does not claim that every global analytic boundary-value problem is thereby solved.

title: The universal pointed curve and its dimensions
notes: The diagram \(X\to M\) has a genus-\(g\) curve as fiber; the displayed dimension is \(6g-6\).
statement: For \(g\ge2\), the smooth moduli stack \(\mathcal M_g\) has complex dimension \(3g-3\), hence real dimension \(6g-6\). Its universal curve is \(\mathcal M_{g,1}\to\mathcal M_g\), with total complex dimension \(3g-2\). On a coarse moduli space a universal family need not exist without a level structure or stack interpretation.
reconstruction: The genus restriction, complex versus real dimension, and stack interpretation are supplied.
fate: This is classical moduli theory, used explicitly in \citet[Sec. 1.1 and Sec. 4.2]{benzvifrenkel2004geometric}. The notebook dimension is correct only as a real dimension of the base.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Cotangent and Hodge determinant line twists
notes: For integers \(j,c\), the fiber at \((K,x)\) is \((\Omega^1_{K,x})^{\otimes j}\otimes[\det\Omega^1(K)]^c\).
statement: On \(\mathcal M_{g,1}\), write \(\psi\) for the cotangent line at the marked point and \(\lambda=\det\pi_*\omega_\pi\) for the Hodge line pulled back from \(\mathcal M_g\). The displayed bundle is \(\psi^{\otimes j}\otimes\lambda^{\otimes c}\), with negative integral powers interpreted as duals. A complex central parameter generally defines a twist of differential operators, not an ordinary fractional tensor power of a line bundle.
reconstruction: The notation \(\Omega^1(K)\) is interpreted as the finite-dimensional space of global holomorphic differentials. The exponent \(c\) is not identified numerically with a Virasoro central charge without fixing the central-extension convention.
fate: \citet{beilinsonschechtman1988determinant}, received 12 February 1988 and published that December, develops determinant bundles and Virasoro action. \citet[Sec. 4.2]{benzvifrenkel2004geometric} treats both actual line bundles and arbitrary complex twists.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Formal-coordinate uniformization and the Virasoro lift
notes: The space \(\widehat X\ni(K,x,q)\) carries an action of formal vector fields; \(t\mathbb C[[t]]\partial_t\) changes the coordinate and the remaining modes vary the curve.
statement: The formal-coordinate torsor over \(\mathcal M_{g,1}\) has a transitive infinitesimal action of \(\operatorname{Der}\mathbb C((t))\), compatible with the coordinate-change group \(\operatorname{Aut}\mathbb C[[t]]\). The central generator acts trivially on the base; the lift to determinant-line differential operators is governed by the Virasoro central extension. This is an infinitesimal algebraic statement, not a global action of an unspecified infinite-dimensional Lie group.
reconstruction: The distinction between the centerless action on coordinates and the central lift on a line twist makes the notebook shorthand precise.
fate: The directly corresponding publication is \citet{beilinsonschechtman1988determinant}. The action and its determinant-line lift are stated and used in \citet[Sec. 1.1 and Prop. 4.2.3]{benzvifrenkel2004geometric}, first circulated January 2003. The precise independent Kontsevich priority is recorded from the notebook, without an identified separate manuscript. \citet[Thm. 1.1]{esnaulttsai2000determinant}, circulated October 1999 and published in 2000, corrects the original paper\textquotesingle s Theorem 2.3.1(ii), a divisor-twist reduction step; this later repair does not invalidate the uniformization principle.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Kodaira--Spencer tangent space through punctured-curve vector fields
notes: The tangent quotient is written as \(\mathit{Vir}/\Phi_q(\mathcal T(K\backslash X))\), then with the point \(x\) in the denominator; two horizontal lifts are compared.
statement: For a smooth pointed curve \(C,p\) with formal coordinate \(q\), the tangent space to the coordinate torsor is the quotient \(\operatorname{Der}\mathbb C((q))/H^0(C\setminus\{p\},T_C)\), where algebraic vector fields have finite-order poles at \(p\) and are expanded in \(q\). Comparing trivializations of an infinitesimal deformation on the formal disc and punctured complement gives the quotient; changing the complement lift adds a global punctured-curve vector field.
reconstruction: The correct point removal, algebraic rather than arbitrary holomorphic vector fields, and finite Laurent pole condition are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 4.2]{benzvifrenkel2004geometric} gives the uniformization and stabilizer formulation. The notebook itself explains the two-lift mechanism. The capital \(X\) in the first denominator is incompatible with the adjoining definitions.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Singular Virasoro vectors produce canonical differential operators
notes: A reducible Verma module \(M_{(c,g)}\) contains a highest-weight vector \(v^{\prime}=L(v)\); applying \(L\in U(\mathit{Vir})\) to a lifted section gives an equation between line twists.
statement: Given a singular vector of definite grade in a Virasoro highest-weight module, localization on the formal-coordinate torsor, followed by equivariant descent, produces a differential operator between the appropriate twisted sheaves. Contragredient conventions determine the direction and weight shift. The construction requires compatibility with the coordinate-change action; a section is represented by an equivariant function, not literally by a single vector of a fixed Verma module.
reconstruction: The highest weight written \(g\) is renamed \(h\) when needed to avoid confusing it with curve genus. No unrecorded central-charge-to-Hodge-power formula is imposed.
fate: The genus-zero null-vector mechanism occurs in \citet{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite}. Its moduli-space globalization belongs to \citet{beilinsonschechtman1988determinant}; \citet[Secs. 2.2--2.4 and 4.2]{benzvifrenkel2004geometric} gives a precise localization framework.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Finite-rank solution local systems require a specified conformal-block sector
notes: The closing sentence says that solutions of the singular-vector equations form a finite-rank local system.
statement: A system of differential equations gives a finite-rank local system on a smooth locus when its corresponding differential module is an integrable connection of finite rank there. Mere reducibility of one arbitrary Virasoro Verma module does not establish this property. To identify the intended conformal-block theorem one needs the representations, insertions, quotient relations, and finiteness hypotheses, none of which are recorded.
reconstruction: The missing finiteness condition is exposed rather than supplied by silently choosing a minimal model.
fate: The null-vector equations of \citet{belavinpolyakovzamolodchikov1984infinite} and localization of \citet{beilinsonschechtman1988determinant} explain the context. They are not evidence for an unconditional finite-rank theorem for every reducible Verma module.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 finite-rank conformal-block systems exist under substantial additional hypotheses, but this particular unrestricted closing assertion is insufficiently specified.

title: Bosonic action and Gaussian surfaces on triangulations
notes: The continuum expression integrates \(X:S\to\mathbb R^n\) and a metric \(g\), then replaces it by a sum over triangulations with an edge energy \(\sum_{i\sim j}|x_i-x_j|^2\).
statement: For a fixed finite connected triangulation, assign target vectors to vertices and a positive quadratic graph energy. A random-surface model sums the resulting Gaussian integrals over a specified map class with area and symmetry weights. The formal continuum Polyakov integral additionally needs a measure, gauge fixing, and treatment of zero modes; the displayed discretization is not a proved equality of continuum measures.
reconstruction: The graph class, weights, and distinction between a finite Gaussian model and a formal metric integral are supplied.
fate: \citet{polyakov1981quantum} gives the continuum motivation. \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces}, circulated as PR-1123 in September 1986 and published 29 December 1986, analyzes this dynamical-triangulation model.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Vertex area weights are not curvature defects
notes: The notes set \(\sigma_i=n_i/3\), call it a defect, and explain it by dividing each regular triangle among its three vertices.
statement: If each equilateral triangle has unit area and \(n_i\) triangles meet at vertex \(i\), its barycentric area allocation is \(n_i/3\), and summing these allocations counts faces. The angular curvature defect is instead \(2\pi-n_i\pi/3\) at an interior vertex. The two quantities encode different geometric data.
reconstruction: The elementary incidence and angle calculation is an editorial correction, explicitly marked as ours.
fate: The discrete area and curvature observables are distinguished in \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces}. \ours\ Counting triangle--vertex incidences gives the area identity and directly explains the notebook diagram; it does not turn \(n_i/3\) into an angle defect.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Piecewise affine Dirichlet energy and the equilateral restriction
notes: The integrands are said to agree for regular embeddings, and a fixed metric with a linear map on each triangle is proposed.
statement: For a piecewise affine map on a Euclidean triangulated surface, its Dirichlet energy is a sum of edge squared differences weighted by cotangents of the opposite angles, up to the chosen factor \(1/2\). Equilateral triangles make these weights constant. For an arbitrary intrinsic triangulation the unweighted graph energy is a different discretization; target images being equilateral is not the necessary intrinsic-metric condition.
reconstruction: The intrinsic domain metric is separated from the shape of its target image; the edge-energy constant must be fixed before claiming equality.
fate: The dynamical-triangulation model of \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces} fixes regular intrinsic triangles. The statement in the notes is a normalization-level discretization observation, not a theorem of convergence to the continuum path integral.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Gauge topology does not require abandoning cubic lattices
notes: Gelfand asks how to write Yang--Mills when characteristic classes appear, saying that one cannot restrict to a cubic lattice.
statement: The relevant precise issue is a geometric definition of topological charge for lattice gauge fields with a controlled continuum limit. A hypercubic cellulation does not preclude such a definition: admissibility or small-curvature restrictions can separate topological sectors. The notebook does not specify a different proposed characteristic-class discretization.
reconstruction: The topological-charge formulation is the narrowest concrete interpretation supported by the intervention; it is not an invented general open gauge problem.
fate: \citet{luscher1982topology}, circulated June 1981 and published in 1982, constructs an integer topological charge for sufficiently small-action-density \(SU(2)\) fields on a four-dimensional hypercubic lattice, invariant under continuous admissible deformations and converging to the continuum Chern number. Thus the claimed obstruction to cubic lattices is too strong.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: High-dimensional concentration does not make every graph triangle equilateral
notes: Zakharevich says a random embedding of any triangulated sphere makes all its triangles regular on average, appealing to concentration near a shell.
statement: Independent identically distributed isotropic vertex vectors can have pair distances concentrated at a common scale in large target dimension. Coordinates distributed by a graph Gaussian, however, have edge variances determined by the graph covariance and effective resistances; those variances need not be equal. A shell-concentration slogan alone therefore does not justify the asserted equilateral replacement.
reconstruction: The two different random-embedding laws are distinguished editorially; no new asymptotic result is claimed.
fate: \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces} studies limiting target dimensions, but its verified abstract does not supply this universal equilateral theorem. No probability law, limit, or error estimate is stated in the notebook.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 concentration statements are available for specified distributions; this unrestricted heuristic is not an identified theorem.
speaker: I. S. Zakharevich

title: Target-dimension factorization and removal of translation modes
notes: The \(n\)-dimensional embedding integral is written as the \(n\)-th power of a one-dimensional Gaussian integral; the parameter \(n\) is then continued analytically.
statement: Fix one vertex of a connected graph and write its scalar energy as \(x^{\mathsf T}L_*x\), with positive reduced Laplacian \(L_*\). The scalar integral is \(\pi^{(v-1)/2}(\det L_*)^{-1/2}\), and \(n\) independent coordinates give its \(n\)-th power for integer \(n\ge0\). The positive determinant permits a specified entire exponential in complex \(n\) for each fixed graph. Analyticity of an infinite map sum requires separate convergence control.
reconstruction: The pinned vertex and measure normalization are explicit editorial repairs; the unpinned integral is infinite.
fate: The Gaussian-embedding model is the one analyzed by \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces}. \ours\ Diagonalizing \(L_*\) gives the displayed finite Gaussian factor and exposes the missing translational zero-mode removal.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: I. S. Zakharevich

title: The solvable dimensions zero and minus two
notes: Kazakov says the sum can be calculated at \(n=0\) and \(n=-2\).
statement: At \(n=0\) the matter determinant disappears, leaving weighted pure planar maps. At \(n=-2\), after fixing the Gaussian normalization, the weight contains \(\det L_*\); the matrix-tree theorem identifies this determinant with the number of spanning trees of the graph. Negative target dimension is determinant analytic continuation, not a Euclidean embedding in a negative-dimensional space.
reconstruction: The determinant interpretation supplies the precise meaning of the formal negative dimension; the word only is retained as a 1986 contextual remark, not an eternal no-go theorem.
fate: Pure-map solvability is explicit in \citet[Sec. 4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar}. \citet{boulatovkazakovkostovmigdal1986surfaces} identifies \(D=-2\) as exactly solvable and reports its logarithmic mean-square-size behavior. The article appeared in December 1986 after September preprint circulation.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Rational map weights and the apparent noninteger counting formula
notes: The cubic series is first called an unlabelled count. At \(k=100\), \(72^{100}149!/(102!50!)\) is observed not to be an integer. Zakharevich replaces the count by a labelled count divided by \(n!\).
statement: Connected matrix free energies enumerate maps with inverse-automorphism weights, so rational coefficients are expected. For a labelling set on which the combinatorial automorphism action is faithful, the orbit--stabilizer relation gives \(\#\{\text{labelled maps}\}/n!=\sum_{[T]}1/|\operatorname{Aut}T|\). The exact labels must include the flag or cyclic-order data used by the Feynman model. The negative sign in the repeated series belongs to the source convention for negative free energy, not a positive counting function.
reconstruction: The weighting and sign conventions repair the count; triangle labels alone are not asserted to remove every possible residual automorphism.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2 and 4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} gives the graph weights and cubic series. \oursComputed\ The 5-adic valuation of the displayed \(k=100\) rational number is \(-1\), confirming its nonintegrality; the exact check is saved with the chapter evidence.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: V. A. Kazakov and I. S. Zakharevich

title: Critical exponents survive only regular changes of coupling
notes: The notes transfer a \(5/2\) singularity in \(b\) to one in \(\beta\), although \(b=b(\beta)\) is not evaluated; the coefficient power is \(-7/2\).
statement: The singular exponent transfers unchanged if \(b(\beta)\) is analytic near criticality and \(b^{\prime}(\beta_*)\ne0\). If its first nonzero derivative has order \(m\), the composed singularity instead has power \(5m/2\). The coefficient asymptotic \(k^{-7/2}\) pertains to the weighted unrooted pure-map series, with its parity convention, and includes an exponential growth factor.
reconstruction: Analytic background terms and the nonvanishing derivative condition are supplied; the note does not determine \(b(\beta)\).
fate: \citet[Sec. 4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} establishes the cubic singularity. \ours\ Substituting the first nonzero term of the Taylor expansion of \(b-b_*\) gives the necessary change-of-variable qualification.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Normalized planar logarithm and higher-valency map potentials
notes: The displayed generating function is \(Z=\lim_{N\to\infty}\log I_N\); the potential may be extended from cubic to cubic plus quartic.
statement: The connected planar free energy is the formal limit \(\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-2}\log[I_N(g,\lambda)/I_N(0,0)]\), with a fixed Gaussian normalization. A term \(\operatorname{tr}M^k\) inserts a vertex of valency \(k\) in the dual ribbon graph. Cubic and quartic terms therefore mix triangle and quadrilateral faces in the dual map. A positive stabilizing leading coefficient gives a convergent real integral; an unstable cubic potential alone remains formal.
reconstruction: The factor \(N^{-2}\), Gaussian denominator, and potential sign conditions repair the displayed limit.
fate: \citet[Secs. 2--4]{brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar} treats these matrix integrals and the planar expansion. This repeats 1986-682.2--.3, with an additional quartic coupling.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Two diagonal source terms and the principal chiral model
notes: Equation (12) has \(\operatorname{tr}(p_1U^{-1}p_1U)+\operatorname{tr}(p_2U^{-1}p_2U)\), with diagonal \(p_1,p_2\), and is identified with a two-dimensional principal chiral field at large \(N\).
statement: For finite \(N\) and specified source matrices the compact integral is entire in the couplings, and its Taylor coefficients are exactly given by unitary Weingarten calculus. A planar chiral-field equivalence additionally needs a prescribed source eigenvalue distribution, scaling, and a justified reduction or quenching procedure. Exact field-theory information does not automatically evaluate the unspecified finite integral.
reconstruction: The distinction between an exact compact integral and a continuum planar equivalence is editorial; the latter is not assigned an artificial solved status.
fate: \citet[Cor. 2.4]{collinssniady2006integration} supplies a convergent finite-\(N\) coefficient method. This is the same two-source integral family as 1986-688.5 and GP-1986-60; the chapter development gives explicit bounded coefficients and a remainder estimate.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 exact finite-dimensional coefficient evaluation is established; the notebook does not specify a unique continuum reduction theorem.

title: Three-state spins and a three-matrix potential
notes: Equation (13) uses three Hermitian matrices, symmetric pair couplings, and quartic self-interactions, with \(Z_3\) spins said to replace Ising spins.
statement: Three matrix species with equal unlike-species covariance encode a three-state Potts interaction on the corresponding ribbon graphs. A quartic vertex generates four-valent dual graphs, so calling the same model a sum of purely triangular dual faces needs correction or a duality convention. With the printed sign, a positive quartic coupling destabilizes the real integral; the Feynman expansion is formal.
reconstruction: The Potts interpretation, graph valency, and formal-integral qualification prevent a false exact publication match.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1]{daul1995potts}, written November 1994 and posted February 1995, treats the \(q\)-state random-planar Potts matrix model and computes three-state scaling information. Its displayed potential is cubic; it is not an exact all-coupling evaluation of the notebook quartic integral.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Angular variables around a three-matrix cycle are constrained
notes: After diagonalization, equation (14) integrates three pairwise angular matrices independently and its final factor is again \(\mu\).
statement: If \(M_i=V_i\Lambda_iV_i^*\), set \(U_{12}=V_1^*V_2\), \(U_{23}=V_2^*V_3\), \(U_{31}=V_3^*V_1\). Then \(U_{12}U_{23}U_{31}=I\); only two are independent after removing common conjugation. The third spectral pair is \(\nu,\lambda\), not a second \(\nu,\mu\) pair. A product of three independent HCIZ integrals therefore gives a different model.
reconstruction: The shared-unitary constraint and final eigenvalue factor are repaired; the scan confirms the repeated \(\mu\) is the literal reading.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1, discussion preceding Eq. (3)]{daul1995potts} explicitly identifies the lack of independence of cyclic relative angles and introduces an auxiliary Gaussian matrix to remove the coupling obstruction. \ours\ The displayed closure identity follows by multiplying the three relative matrices.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The higher-dimensional gauge integral recurs
notes: The one-site unitary plaquette integral is repeated; \(d=2\) is called solved and \(d=3,4\) are requested.
statement: The problem is the nonperturbative planar free energy and Wilson-loop observables of a fixed \(d\)-matrix plaquette model in dimensions three and four, together with a justified center-symmetric volume-reduction regime. The printed action also needs a real part, or an explicit sum over both plaquette orientations, for the usual real Euclidean gauge weight.
reconstruction: The phase, orientation convention, and symmetry conditions are needed to formulate the literal target accurately.
fate: \citet{eguchikawai1982reduction} is the original reduction; \citet[Secs. 1--2]{garciaperez2020largeN} explains the center-symmetry obstruction and modern variants. This is a repeat of GP-1986-31, not a new independent problem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the general three- and four-dimensional analytic planar solution is not supplied by the established reduction methods; the original weak-coupling four-dimensional untwisted equivalence fails.
worth: Worth a bounded coefficient or symmetry calculation for a specified model; the unrestricted all-coupling higher-dimensional planar solution is a much larger target.

title: Projective geometries and continuous geometries as lattice antecedents
notes: Gelfand lists Dedekind, Weyl on projective axioms, and von Neumann on factors; dimension is described by lengths of chains, with Desargues in dimension at least three.
statement: The lattice of subspaces of an \(n\)-dimensional vector space is complemented and modular with maximal strict-chain length \(n\). Projective dimension is \(n-1\). Incidence projective spaces of projective dimension at least three are Desarguesian; arbitrary projective planes need not be. Von Neumann continuous geometries replace finite rank by a continuous dimension theory under additional lattice-completeness conditions.
reconstruction: The vector-space/projective-dimension shift and the distinction between finite projective geometry and continuous geometry are made explicit.
fate: The coordinatization framework is developed and precisely recalled in \citet[Introduction and Sec. 2]{herrmann1984arithmetic}. The notebook compresses several classical theories and does not specify the separate work attributed to the uncertain name Disona.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Two and three subspaces: finite indecomposable types
notes: Two subspaces are called trivial; three decompose into one-dimensional pieces and a configuration of three lines. The associated free modular lattice has 28 elements.
statement: An ordered triple of subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space over a field decomposes into one-dimensional blocks, each subspace being zero or the entire line, and copies of the two-dimensional block of three distinct lines. The decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and order of blocks. Separately, the abstract free modular lattice on three generators has 28 elements; this counts lattice terms modulo modular identities, not indecomposable representation types.
reconstruction: The field, ordering, finite dimension, and difference between lattice-element and representation counts are supplied.
fate: \citet[Opening paragraph]{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples} recalls the elementary two- and three-subspace cases. \citet[p. 513]{herrmann1983four} confirms the 28-element free modular lattice. These facts long precede the talk.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Four-subspace classification and its parameter families
notes: The four-subspace problem is attributed to long work of Gelfand and Ponomarev, with a reference to Manin.
statement: Classify ordered quadruples of subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space up to a common linear isomorphism. The category admits direct-sum decomposition into indecomposables and an explicit classification containing discrete families and regular one-parameter data. Over a general field, irreducible polynomial and rational-canonical data replace eigenvalue parameters; the classification is not a finite list of configurations.
reconstruction: Field-dependent regular parameters are retained, rather than assuming an algebraically closed field without saying so.
fate: \citet{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples}, received 21 October 1970, gives the matching canonical classification; it was already reported in earlier seminar record 1970-198. The 1986 passage is retrospective.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The free modular lattice and its linear representations
notes: Terms in \(e_1,\ldots,e_r\) use sum and intersection, with equality by axioms; a representation preserves both operations.
statement: Let \(D^r\) be the free lattice in the variety of modular lattices on \(r\) generators. A finite-dimensional linear representation over \(k\) is a lattice homomorphism \(\rho:D^r\to L(V)\), with \(L(V)\) the subspace lattice. Thus a representation is exactly a configuration of \(r\) ordered subspaces of \(V\), extended to all lattice terms. Abstract equality in \(D^r\) need not be the same relation as equality in every such representation.
reconstruction: The field and finite-dimensional representation category are specified.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1, pp. 524--525]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} states these definitions. The project builds on \citet{gelfandponomarev1974modular}.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Undecidable equality in free modular lattices
notes: The notes say the word-identity problem is undecidable for \(r\ge5\).
statement: There is no algorithm deciding whether two lattice terms are equal in the free modular lattice on \(r\) generators when \(r\ge4\). The result concerns equality modulo all modular identities, not equality in all finite-dimensional subspace lattices over a fixed field.
reconstruction: The distinct decision problems are separated; Ryzhikova\textquotesingle s theorem is not a contradiction of the free-modular-lattice result.
fate: \citet[Thm. 1, p. 513]{herrmann1983four} proves the four-generator case and recalls Freese\textquotesingle s earlier \(r\ge5\) theorem. The note is correct but gives a nonoptimal threshold already in 1986. \citet[Theorem]{ryzhikova1987decidability} establishes the contrasting decidability of subspace-lattice identities, submitted 16 May 1986 and published in 1987.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Finite equational axiomatization of linear equivalence
notes: Ryzhikova, Semenov\textquotesingle s diploma student, is associated with the question whether linear equivalence can be formulated by finitely many axioms.
statement: In the equational interpretation, ask whether all identities valid in subspace lattices of finite-dimensional rational vector spaces follow from finitely many lattice identities. Equivalently, is the lattice variety generated by these subspace lattices finitely based? The analogous class including all fields contains the rational case and is also generated by finite-dimensional lattices. The notebook does not fix a field or say whether axioms must be equations.
reconstruction: The equational and field quantifiers are explicit editorial specifications. This is not the earlier decidability problem GP-1985-20.
fate: \citet[Thm. 1.4]{herrmann1984arithmetic}, received February 1982 and revised August 1983, proves that a modular variety containing all rational projective geometries cannot both be finitely based and be generated by its finite-dimensional members. This gives a negative answer to the stated standard interpretation. \citet{ryzhikova1987decidability} answers a different question, algorithmic recognition, affirmatively.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the finite equational basis question under the rational/all-field interpretation has a pre-1986 negative answer. Fixed positive-characteristic variants or unrestricted first-order axioms are not silently identified with this formulation.

title: Morphisms and indecomposability of lattice representations
notes: A morphism \(V_1\to V_2\) takes every represented subspace into its counterpart; indecomposability is introduced through direct sums.
statement: For representations \(\rho_i:D^r\to L(V_i)\), define \(\operatorname{Hom}(\rho_1,\rho_2)=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(V_1,V_2):f(\rho_1(x))\subseteq\rho_2(x)\ \forall x\in D^r\}\). It suffices to impose the inclusions on the generators. A direct-sum splitting must split all represented subspaces simultaneously; indecomposable means no nontrivial such splitting.
reconstruction: The requirement of simultaneous splitting prevents confusion with arbitrary decompositions of the ambient vector space.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1, p. 525]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} gives exactly this category. It is the standard category underlying the earlier subspace-configuration work.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Preprojective means finiteness of source types, not finiteness of morphisms
notes: The page break gives a definition ending with only finitely many morphisms \(\tau:\rho\to\rho_0\).
statement: A representation \(\rho_0\) is preprojective in this finite-dimensional subspace category when only finitely many isomorphism classes of indecomposable \(\rho\) have \(\operatorname{Hom}(\rho,\rho_0)\ne0\). Over an infinite field every nonzero Hom space itself has infinitely many scalar multiples; counting individual morphisms would therefore destroy the intended definition. Arnold\textquotesingle s phrase without parameters is an intuition, not an equivalent categorical definition.
reconstruction: The fixed target, indecomposable source, nonzero Hom condition, and isomorphism-class quotient are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1, definition and Prop. 1]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} supplies the intended representation-type finiteness. The actual scan confirms the notebook says morphisms, so the repair is mathematical rather than paleographic.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Explicit classification of preprojective representations
notes: Theorem 1 says all preprojective representations of a free lattice on an uncertain \(r\) or (4) generators are described.
statement: For the free modular lattice \(D^r\) in the range considered by the published paper, the indecomposable preprojective representations consist of the zero-valued one-dimensional representation \(\rho_{0,0}\) and explicitly indexed representations \(\rho_{t,l}\) constructed from homogeneous pieces of a graded algebra \(A_k^r\). The algebraic construction works over a specified field \(k\); it does not classify all indecomposable \(r\)-subspace systems.
reconstruction: The uncertain handwritten generator count is not forcibly read as four. The modern statement specifies the preprojective subcategory and cites the explicit algebraic index rather than claiming a full wild-type classification.
fate: \citet[Sec. 2, Prop. 6]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective}, received 9 December 1986 and published in 1987, gives the exact classification and points to earlier Gelfand--Ponomarev constructions. This is a direct publication match to the announced description.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: The preprojective quotient and its representation category
notes: Identify lattice elements when every preprojective representation has the same value. Theorem 2 says the preprojective representations of the lattice and its reduction coincide.
statement: Over \(\mathbb Q\), define \(x\sim_{\mathrm{pp}}y\) when \(\rho(x)=\rho(y)\) for every indecomposable preprojective representation, and let \(P_{\mathbb Q}D^r=D^r/\sim_{\mathrm{pp}}\). The equivalence is a lattice congruence. The published classification of all indecomposable representations of this quotient consists of the original preprojective representations together with the dual all-full one-dimensional representation \(\rho_{0,0}^{\prime}\). Thus a statement about all quotient representations needs this extra object.
reconstruction: The rational ground field and the distinction between preprojective representations and all quotient representations are supplied.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1, definition and Prop. 5]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} gives this precise quotient statement. The notebook\textquotesingle s narrower assertion about preprojectives is compatible with it, but does not itself state the all-representation classification.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Describe the lattice obtained by preprojective reduction
notes: The problem of finding the reduction is marked will be done and then actually already done.
statement: For \(D^r\) over \(\mathbb Q\), describe exactly which families \(U_\rho\subset V_\rho\), indexed by nontrivial indecomposable preprojectives, arise as \(U_\rho=\rho(x)\) for one lattice element \(x\). In the large-rank range of the published theorem, the criterion is compatibility \(\sum_{\tau<\rho}U_\tau\operatorname{Hom}(\tau,\rho)\subseteq U_\rho\), with equality for all but finitely many \(\rho\). Equivalently the quotient is described by finitely generated positive-degree homogeneous right ideals of the explicit graded algebra.
reconstruction: The family-compatibility criterion is reconstructed from the published theorem; the notebook contains only the announcement. The conservative rank subrange avoids silently guessing an OCR inequality.
fate: \citet[Thms. 1A--1C]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} publishes the announced description in 1987. The rank condition is essential: its following remark says the assertion is false at \(r=4\) and had not been proved there for \(r=5\). We use the criterion only for \(r\ge7\), a safe subrange of the OCR-rendered condition \(r>6\); the precise endpoint requires a cleaner scan of the paper. The endpoint \(r=6\) is unresolved in our source verification only; no assertion that it is mathematically open is made.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the published large-rank rational description is established. The 1987 rank-five gap is a historical limitation of that theorem, not evidence that a rank-five problem remains open today.

title: Perfect elements are tested on indecomposable representations
notes: A perfect element is defined by \(\rho(a)=0\) or \(V\) for every representation, and compared to the center of a group ring.
statement: The standard definition requires \(\rho(a)\in\{0,V\}\) for every indecomposable finite-dimensional representation, over the fields under consideration. On a decomposable representation different summands may take different alternatives, so the image can be a proper nonzero direct summand. The analogy with central idempotents concerns such block selection; it is not an isomorphism of lattice and ring centers.
reconstruction: The omitted indecomposable restriction is a substantive correction confirmed against the original P001327 scan.
fate: \citet{gelfandponomarev1974modular} introduced these perfect elements. \citet[Sec. 1, Prop. 3 and following discussion]{gelfandlidskiiponomarev1987preprojective} restates the indecomposable qualifier and the construction from suitable upward-closed subsets of preprojectives.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Unitary characters of the complex multiplicative group
notes: \(\delta(z)=(z/|z|)^k|z|^{i\rho}\), \(k\in\mathbb Z\), \(\rho\in\mathbb R\), and \(u(\delta,n)=\delta\circ\det\).
statement: Every continuous unitary character of \(\mathbb C^\times\) has the displayed form, using the ordinary complex modulus. Composing with determinant gives a one-dimensional unitary representation of \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb C)\). These are the \(u(\delta,n)\) building blocks in the complex-field classification because square-integrable representations modulo center occur here only for \(\operatorname{GL}_1(\mathbb C)\).
reconstruction: Continuity and the ordinary-modulus convention are specified.
fate: \citet[Secs. 1.2 and 9.1]{badulescurenard2010unitary} explicitly gives these blocks and places them in the established Tadić--Vogan classification. The characters themselves are classical.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Stein complementary-series blocks and the complex absolute value
notes: The second family is induced from \(|\det|^\alpha u(\delta,n)\otimes|\det|^{-\alpha}u(\delta,n)\), with \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
statement:
Let \(
u(g)=|\det g|_{\mathbb C}=|\det g|^2\), where the rightmost modulus is ordinary. With normalized parabolic induction, \(\pi(u,\alpha)=
u^\alpha u	imes
u^{-\alpha}u\) is irreducible and unitarizable for \(0<\alpha<1/2\). If ordinary modulus is used directly, the corresponding exponent interval is \(0<a<1\). The completion uses an invariant positive form; the naively twisted inducing characters are not themselves unitary.
reconstruction: The normalized local absolute value and the modular factor in induction are indispensable; the notebook uses the same bars as in its ordinary-modulus character formula without defining the change.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1.2 and Thm. 7.2]{badulescurenard2010unitary} states the precise complex normalization. \citet{vogan1986unitary}, published October 1986, establishes the surrounding Archimedean classification before this talk.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Induction, modular normalization, and the relevant adjunction
notes: Gelfand defines induced functions by \(f(hg)=\pi(h)f(g)\), then says restriction and induction are dual functors.
statement: For parabolic \(P=MN\) in a reductive local group, normalized smooth induction uses an equivariance factor \(\delta_P^{1/2}\) in addition to the inducing \(M\)-representation, with a consistent left/right convention. In the non-Archimedean smooth category its Frobenius adjunction involves the normalized Jacquet functor, not merely ordinary restriction to \(M\). For finite groups ordinary induction and restriction satisfy the familiar Frobenius reciprocity. Function spaces and completions matter for locally compact groups.
reconstruction: The categorical and analytic qualifications distinguish an informal induction definition from the precise parabolic functor.
fate: \citet[Sec. 1]{tadic1986classification} and \citet[Secs. 2.4--3]{badulescurenard2010unitary} fix the normalized parabolic conventions used in the classification. The notebook gives only the underlying equivariant-function picture.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Irreducibility, exhaustiveness, and uniqueness of the complex unitary building blocks
notes: Theorem (5) says all products of the two block types are irreducible and unitary, every irreducible unitary representation occurs, and equivalence means permutation of blocks.
statement: For \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb C)\), take a finite multiset of determinant-character blocks \(u(\delta,m)\) and complementary blocks \(\pi(u(\delta,m),\alpha)\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), whose degrees sum to \(n\). Their normalized parabolic product is irreducible and unitarizable. Every irreducible unitary representation occurs, and the multiset of blocks is unique. This classifies irreducibles; general unitary representations require direct-integral multiplicity data.
reconstruction: Normalized induction, the local absolute value, and irreducibility rather than arbitrary unitary decompositions are specified.
fate: \citet{vogan1986unitary} was published in October 1986. The Tadić approach circulated as MPI/SFB 85--22 in 1985; \citet[Secs. 1.2, 7.2 and 12]{badulescurenard2010unitary} gives the precise theorem and later proof history, including the separate ingredients needed for the Archimedean approach.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Square integrability must be taken modulo the center
notes: \(D^u\) is the set of square-integrable representations of \(\operatorname{GL}_k(F)\), with square-integrable matrix coefficients.
statement: The relevant building blocks are irreducible unitary representations whose matrix coefficients are square-integrable on \(\operatorname{GL}_k(F)/Z\), with unitary central character. They need not be square-integrable on the full group, whose center is noncompact. For \(F=\mathbb C\), only \(k=1\) occurs; for \(F=\mathbb R\), \(k=1,2\) occur; non-Archimedean local fields have higher-degree discrete-series blocks.
reconstruction: The omitted center quotient is substantive and is restored explicitly.
fate: \citet[Secs. 7 and 9]{badulescurenard2010unitary} uses square integrability modulo center throughout. \citet[Sec. 5]{tadic1986classification} gives the non-Archimedean Langlands ingredients.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Speh blocks as Langlands quotients and the correct segment
notes: \(u(\delta,n)\) is the unique irreducible quotient of an induction with first exponent \((n-1)/2\), second \(n/2-1\), and final exponent \(-(n-1)/2\) without a final \(\delta\).
statement:
For an irreducible unitary square-integrable-mod-center representation \(\delta\) of \(\operatorname{GL}_k(F)\), with \(F\) a local field, set \(u(\delta,n)\) to be the unique Langlands quotient of \(
u^{(n-1)/2}\delta	imes
u^{(n-3)/2}\delta	imes\cdots	imes
u^{-(n-1)/2}\delta\). Here \(
u=|\det|_F\) and the exponents decrease by one. The standard module is generally reducible; its quotient is the block used in the unitary classification.
reconstruction: The scan confirms the second exponent \(n/2-1\), so replacing it by \((n-3)/2\) is a faithful-error correction, not a transcription claim; the last \(\delta\) is restored.

title: The field-uniform classification is a theorem for local fields
notes: The notes say the same theorem remains valid for every field after replacing characters by \(D^u\).
statement: For a nondiscrete locally compact field \(F\), the split general linear unitary dual is parametrized by normalized products of \(u(\delta,n)\) and \(\nu^\alpha u(\delta,n)\times\nu^{-\alpha}u(\delta,n)\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), with unique block multisets. The topology, Haar measure, and admissible smooth or Harish-Chandra category are part of the theorem. It is not a theorem about arbitrary abstract fields without topology.
reconstruction: The local-field qualification repairs the phrase every field; finite groups of rational points are a separate representation problem.
fate: \citet[Theorem A and Sec. 7]{tadic1986classification} proves the non-Archimedean local-field result in 1986. \citet{vogan1986unitary} treats Archimedean groups; \citet[Thm. 7.2 and its hypotheses]{badulescurenard2010unitary} unifies the block formulation.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Claims about other groups lack a fixed real form
notes: Gelfand asks about other groups. Kirillov lists \(B_2=C_2\), \(G_2\), \(SU(2,2)\), \(SU(2,n)\), and names Knapp and Duflo; \(SO(5)\sim Sp(4)\) is written.
statement: A unitary-dual claim must specify the locally compact group, its real or complex form, covering group, and central character conventions. Root-system symbols \(B_2,C_2,G_2\) do not supply these data. The relation between orthogonal and symplectic rank-two groups is a Lie-algebra or isogeny relation, not an unqualified isomorphism of the displayed global groups. The note contains no parameter list or theorem for the named non-general-linear groups.
reconstruction: The absence of a specified real form is retained as a source limitation instead of silently choosing complex groups.
fate: \citet[References, Knapp--Speh 1983 and Duflo 1980 entries]{vogan1986unitary} identifies relevant pre-existing classification literature, but this is a thematic lead rather than an exact match to every group in the notebook list. No separate open conjecture is inferred.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 the notebook list is too compressed to classify each intended real-form theorem responsibly.

title: Quaternionic general linear groups and reducibility normalization
notes: The final attribution says Vogan did the quaternionic ones.
statement: The unitary dual of \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb H)\) belongs to the Archimedean general-linear classification. Its analogous block construction uses the reduced norm and a reducibility step \(\nu_\delta\) attached to each discrete-series block. One cannot copy the split-field exponents with an undefined quaternionic determinant; in particular the reducibility step changes for one-dimensional \(\mathbb H^\times\) blocks.
reconstruction: The group is inferred from the preceding general-linear context; no claim about all quaternionic classical groups is attributed to the phrase.
fate: \citet{vogan1986unitary} is the established 1986 classification. \citet[Prop. 9.10 and Secs. 10--12]{badulescurenard2010unitary} proves the detailed compatibility with the Tadić block description and explains the exceptional step \(\nu_\delta=\nu^2\) for one-dimensional \(\mathbb H^\times\) blocks.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.

title: Riesz-kernel Hermitian forms and the positive range
notes: Gelfand writes the double integral with kernel \(|x_1-x_2|^{-\rho}\) and says it converges for \(\rho<2\).
statement: On \(\mathbb R^2\simeq\mathbb C\), for a Schwartz function \(f\) and \(0<\rho<2\), the quadratic form \(\iint |x-y|^{-\rho}f(x)\overline{f(y)}\,dx\,dy\) is finite and positive. In the Fourier convention \(\widehat f(\xi)=\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}f(x)dx\), it equals a positive constant times \(\int |\xi|^{\rho-2}|\widehat f(\xi)|^2d\xi\). Local kernel integrability requires \(\rho<2\); positivity and decay assumptions are separate issues.
reconstruction: The ambient real dimension two, Schwartz test space, and lower positivity bound are reconstructed from the threshold; the note does not specify its test-function space.
fate: This is the classical homogeneous-distribution mechanism treated in \citet[Ch. II, Sec. 3]{gelfandshilov1964generalized}; its representation-theoretic application belongs to intertwining-operator theory such as \citet{knappstein1971intertwining}. \ours\ Positivity in the stated range also follows directly by writing \(|x|^{-\rho}=\Gamma(\rho/2)^{-1}\int_0^\infty t^{\rho/2-1}e^{-t|x|^2}dt\) and using the positive Fourier transform of each Gaussian.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026 this is an established result under the hypotheses in the modern statement.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Analytic continuation alone does not preserve positivity
notes: For \(\rho>2\) the notes demand analytic continuation and say the form will no longer be positive definite; a Fourier-side weighted norm is sketched.
statement: The homogeneous kernel admits meromorphic continuation as a tempered distribution, with poles at even positive values of \(\rho\) in real dimension two. Away from poles, its Fourier coefficient is proportional to \(2^{2-\rho}\pi\Gamma(1-\rho/2)/\Gamma(\rho/2)\); its sign depends on the parameter interval and any scalar normalization. Thus continuation is not automatically positive, but the blanket claim of nonpositivity for every \(\rho>2\) is also too strong. Invariant subquotients and moment-vanishing conditions require their own analysis.
reconstruction: The unnormalized continuation, its poles, and scalar sign are distinguished from positivity of a specified representation-theoretic quotient.
fate: \citet[Chs. II--III]{gelfandshilov1964generalized} provides the homogeneous-distribution framework; \citet{knappstein1971intertwining} develops the intertwining and complementary-series context. The notebook gives no specific representation whose positivity range can be fully reconstructed.
